original_text: PhD Position Transition Pathways and Innovation for Circular Consumption of E-bikes and Electronics — Delft University of Technology (TU Delft) — AcademicTransfer For candidates For employers For members AcademicTransfer Jobs and employers Jobs Premium employers Academic employers Universities of Applied Sciences Career journey Orientation Matching Preparation E-learning Events en English (EN) Nederlands (NL) PhD Position Transition Pathways and Innovation for Circular Consumption of E-bikes and Electronics Deadline tomorrow Published 4 Sep ’26 Vacancy ID 3760 Apply now 1 day remaining Save Research fields Engineering; Environmental science Job types PhD Education level University graduate Weekly hours 38 hours per week Salary indication €3204—€4051 per month Location Mekelweg 5, 2628CD, Delft View on Google Maps Job description Do you want to understand how to organise the transition to circular consumption of e-bikes, employing stakeholder workshops, scenarios, and pathways, and diving into circular consumption ecosystems? Job description If this question sparks your interest and you are motivated to pursue a PhD in circular consumption niches and the transition to circular consumption, you might be our new colleague for the Circular Consumption through Value-Chain Integration and Co-Creation for the Circular Economy (CIVIC-4CE) project. We are seeking an excellent candidate for a 4-year PhD study as part of the CIVIC-4CE project, an interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary research project funded by NWO, the Netherlands Research Council, under the call on KIC Consumer behaviour for a circular system transition. See: https://www.tudelft.nl/en/2026/tbm/tpm-researchers-receive-nwo-kic-consumer-behaviour-for-a-circular-system-transition-grant . The project includes 2 PhD positions, 2 Postdoc positions, and several researchers at Universities of Applied Sciences. CIVIC-4CE studies how changing consumer behaviour can accelerate the Dutch transition to a circular society. The project focuses on how changing circular consumption contributes to extending product lifetime, retaining material value, and reducing waste, with cases on e-bikes and electronics (washing machines). Using a transdisciplinary research approach that includes stakeholder engagement, behavioural science, design research, transition studies, and modelling, the project aims to develop empirically grounded interventions and governance strategies that enable lasting behavioural change towards circular consumption. Within this PhD vacancy, you will work in the work package that focuses on systemic transitions towards circular consumption and production through integrating behavioural change, visions and transition pathways, modelling, and policy mixes. The work combines qualitative and quantitative methods, including stakeholder workshops, interviews, backcasting, transition pathways, policy mixes, social simulation modelling, and possibly participatory value evaluation or gamification. You will collaborate with other early-career and senior researchers in the project, as well as other consortium partners. You will also reach out to relevant stakeholders, innovating companies, and policymakers to gather data and validate results. Your main supervisors will be Assistant Professor Jaco Quist and Associate Professor Emile Chappin. Job requirements The following further qualifications will be considered in the assessment, while the profile of the candidate will be taken into account for developing the direction of the research: Documented experiences and skills in one or several types of methods, e.g., qualitative research, participatory research, quantitative socio-technical modelling. Strong background and interest in the transition to a circular economy, circular innovation ecosystems, circular/sustainable consumption and participatory approaches. Ability to thrive in an interdisciplinary and technical environment. Excellent writing, presenting, and communication skills. Open-minded team player, able to work in multidisciplinary teams and to collaborate with stakeholders. The working language in the project is English, so the candidate must have strong skills in both written and spoken English, while sufficient proficiency in Dutch is considered an advantage for stakeholder interactions and research into relevant circular consumption niches. TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference. For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future. At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward. Faculty Technology, Policy & Management The Faculty of TPM provides an important contribution to solving complex technical-social issues, such as energy transition, mobility, digitalisation, water management and (cyber) security. TPM does this with its excellent education and research at the intersection of technology, society and policy. We combine insights from both engineering and social sciences as well as the humanities. TPM develops robust models and designs, is internationally oriented and has an extensive network of knowledge institutions, companies, social organisations and governments. Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Technology, Policy and Management. Conditions of employment Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met. Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204 - €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%. As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills. The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged. Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service , offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands. Additional information For more information about this vacancy, you can contact Dr Jaco Quist ( j.n.quist@tudelft.nl ). Application procedure Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than 30 September 2026 via the application button and upload the following documents: CV, cover letter, BSc/MSc diploma (in English), and grade transcripts, including an official description of the grading scale The first round of interviews will take place on 7 and 9 October, and the second round of interviews is scheduled for 21 October 2026. A concise overview of the project and a description of the WP on “Systemic Transitions towards Circular Consumption and Production: Integrating Behavioural Change, Modelling, and Policy using stakeholder dialogue, pathways and backcasting” are available upon request. Candidates who are invited for an interview will be asked to submit two writing samples, e.g., a paper or a thesis. Candidates who are invited will be requested to prepare first ideas for the PhD project proposal (maximum 2 pages), including a possible research objective, theoretical framework, phases and intended methodological approach. If the applicants are selected for an interview, they will be asked to provide contact details of two referees with their consent. You can address your application to Dr Jaco Quist. Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements . Please note: You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. Gross Monthly salary : 1.900,00 € (including the apportionments of extra payments) Expected starting date : 6 March Workday: Full Time (37.5 hours per week) Employment status: Support technician C Place of Work: Pontevedra The Post-Growth Innovation Lab at the University of Vigo invites applications for a research support technitian in the project A Right to a Repair Society: Controversies, Opportunities, and Challenges (ATTRACT) . This project investigates how the Right to Repair (R2R) movement can contribute to a post-growth society while addressing the environmental and social challenges posed by consumer electronics. The full job offer can be found at the following link: https://secretaria.uvigo.gal/uv/web/convocatoria/public/show/1514 (external link) PROJECT OVERVIEW The Right to Repair (R2R) movement advocates for greater rights and collective freedoms to repair our electronic devices, countering manufacturer practices like planned obsolescence. By promoting repairability, R2R aims to reduce electronic waste, limit resource extraction, and foster sustainable consumption practices. This project will map the multiple perspectives surrounding the R2R debate and analyse how these perspectives influence EU legislation on sustainability and circular economy. While mapping out these different perspectives is essential, the project places a strong focus on how they are being integrated in actual R2R legislation, particularly within the European Union. Finally, the project will analyse these dynamics in terms of their alignment with the transition to a post-growth economy. ATTRACT Project (Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities) Supervisors : Dr. Javier Lloveras (external link) and Dr. Mario Pansera (external link) Project Title : A Right to a Repair Society: Controversies, Opportunities, and Challenges (ATTRACT) Funding Duration : 4 years Gross salary : approx €23000 per year Scholarship type: Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities Expected starting date : December 2024-January 2025 NEW PRE-APPLICATION DEADLINE : 15 October The Post-Growth Innovation Lab at the University of Vigo invites applications for a fully funded PhD position in the project A Right to a Repair Society: Controversies, Opportunities, and Challenges (ATTRACT) . This project investigates how the Right to Repair (R2R) movement can contribute to a post-growth society while addressing the environmental and social challenges posed by consumer electronics. PROJECT OVERVIEW The Right to Repair (R2R) movement advocates for greater rights and collective freedoms to repair our electronic devices, countering manufacturer practices like planned obsolescence. By promoting repairability, R2R aims to reduce electronic waste, limit resource extraction, and foster sustainable consumption practices. This project will map the multiple perspectives surrounding the R2R debate and analyse how these perspectives influence EU legislation on sustainability and circular economy. While mapping out these different perspectives is essential, the project places a strong focus on how they are being integrated in actual R2R legislation , particularly within the European Union . Finally, the project will analyse these dynamics in terms of their alignment with the transition to a post-growth economy. PhD CANDIDATE PROFILE We welcome applicants from any academic background—be it social sciences, humanities, or natural sciences—as long as they possess the necessary skills and motivations required for the project. Below is a detailed list of the essential skills we are looking for. While it’s not necessary to meet every single criterion, these are the qualities we will prioritize when shortlisting candidates. The ideal candidate will have the following essential skills : A good understanding of the EU legislative process in relevant areas. Experience working with qualitative research methods (e.g., interviews, discourse analysis) and a disposition to develop their qualitative research skills further. Critical thinking and ability to review and synthesize academic literature across various disciplines and fields. Experience conducting systematic literature reviews – or at least, a reasonable understanding of this process. A good understanding of postgrowth/degrowth theories. Availability to travel for fieldwork. Proven ability to carry out academic work in English (writing, reading, and speaking). Ability to communicate in Spanish language is not mandatory but advisable. Autonomy, resilience, and an ability to conduct academic work independently. Teamwork skills and the ability to collaborate effectively. ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS · Candidates must hold a Bachelor's degree, or equivalent, and a Master's degree, or equivalent, provided they have completed at least 300 ECTS credits in the two types of programmes as a whole. · We invited candidates from any discipline to apply. RESPONSIBILITIES To work on a full time PhD whose content will be directly aligned with the general project aim and objectives Conduct a rigorous, systematic review of relevant literature Conduct qualitative research, including aspects of research design, fieldwork, and data analysis. Engage with and collect data from multiple stakeholders in the Right to Repair debate in the EU. From consumer groups to policy makers, to activists and NGOs, etc. Contribute to publications, policy briefs, and public outreach as part of the project. BENEFITS Full funding for 4 years . The opportunity to contribute to innovative research at the intersection of sustainability, postgrowth, and EU policy. Access to international academic and policy networks. Support for career development, including opportunities for publication and participation in international conferences. HOW TO APPLY The application process is divided in two stages (pre-application and formal application). Only shortlisted candidates will be asked to formally apply to the University of Vigo, with detailed instructions provided at that stage. Following the formal application process, interviews will be conducted. Deadline for pre-applications is 15 October . The following documents are required for this pre-application (sent to this e-mail address: postgrowth-lab@uvigo.es (external link) ): Curriculum Vitae (CV) highlighting areas that are relevant to the project A cover letter outlining their research interests and motivation for applying, including how their background fits the project At least one reference letter (preferably two) from relevant referees. A brief research proposal (max. 1,000 words) on how they would approach the PhD topic. The following documents will be later required for the shortlisted applicants invited to make formal application : Abbreviated CV, following the standardized format ( https://cvn.fecyt.es/ (external link) ), with specific emphasis on scientific and technical contributions, as well as international experience and mobility. Academic transcripts. Grading scale and equivalencies (external link) (only for those studies completed outside the Spanish system), formally signed by the issuing institution (external link) . This applies only to foreign degrees. Africa , PhD , Scholarships , South America | 0 | Spread the love The University of Bonn and Bonn-Rhein-Sieg University of Applied Sciences are inviting applications for 10 doctoral research positions under the DFG Research Training Group (RTG) “Urban Future – Managing Transformations for Better Health in Blue Cities.” The interdisciplinary doctoral programme focuses on the relationship between urbanisation, water, public health, ecological sustainability and social justice , with particular attention to cities located along rivers and coastlines. Starting in April 2027 , successful candidates will join a structured four-year doctoral programme that combines individual PhD research with interdisciplinary training, seminars, systems-thinking approaches, transdisciplinary research methods and professional development. The programme is particularly relevant to graduates interested in urban health, public health, climate change, water-health systems, governance, environmental sustainability, infectious diseases, urban planning, ecological systems, development studies and social sciences . Successful doctoral researchers will receive a four-year doctoral support contract with remuneration based on TV-L pay grade 13 (65%) , according to the German public-sector salary scale. Employment will be at either the University of Bonn or Bonn-Rhein-Sieg University of Applied Sciences. The application deadline is 19 October 2026 . About the Urban Future Research Training Group The DFG Research Training Group “Urban Future” examines how cities can manage urban transformations in ways that improve public health, ecological sustainability and social equity . The programme uses the concept of the “Blue City” to describe urban areas situated along rivers or coastlines where water is considered more than simply a resource or a potential hazard. Instead, water becomes an integral part of: Urban planning Infrastructure development Environmental management Public health Social systems Urban identity Climate adaptation Ecological sustainability The research programme recognises that cities are complex systems in which environmental, social, economic, political and health-related factors interact. Researchers will therefore investigate the connections between urban transformation, water-related challenges and health outcomes , particularly in rapidly changing urban environments. A major emphasis is placed on cities in the Global South , which serve as important living laboratories for understanding urban transformation and developing solutions that can contribute to healthier and more sustainable cities. However, applicants are not restricted to research sites in the Global South. Candidates are free to propose research sites in any Blue City worldwide , provided that the proposed research aligns with the objectives of the programme. Universities and International Research Network The Research Training Group is jointly operated by: University of Bonn Bonn-Rhein-Sieg University of Applied Sciences It works in cooperation with the German Institute of Development and Sustainability (IDOS) and a network of international partner universities. The international partnership includes institutions in: Ghana Togo Cameroon Brazil Japan The listed partner institutions include: KNUST – Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Ghana University of Ghana, Ghana University of Cape Coast, Ghana University of Lomé, Togo University of Buea, Cameroon University of São Paulo, Brazil The University of Tokyo, Japan This international structure gives doctoral researchers an opportunity to work within a research environment that connects European and Global South perspectives on urban health, sustainability and transformation. Four Research Themes of the Urban Future PhD Programme The doctoral programme is organised around four major interdisciplinary research themes. Research Theme A: Urban Health Resilience The Urban Health Resilience theme examines how urban communities respond to and recover from health pressures associated with water and environmental change. Research may focus on issues such as: Flooding Drought Urban heat islands Air pollution Unequal access to clean water Food systems Environmental exposures Mental health Social inequalities Climate adaptation Green and blue infrastructure The research theme combines perspectives from areas such as epidemiology, sociology, environmental science, urban planning and public health . Researchers will examine how communities can develop greater resilience while ensuring that vulnerable populations are not left behind. Example PhD research topics Potential research areas include: Urban Food Systems Possible methods include: Nutritional analysis Dietary surveys Health outcome measurements Intervention studies Soil Health and Soil Functions Potential methods include: Soil surveys Soil health indicator measurement Ecosystem measurements Functional measurements One Health and Planetary Health Resilience Potential methods include: Human and mental health assessments Environmental exposure measurements Longitudinal studies Spatial analysis Socio-ecological analysis Intervention and transformative studies Urban Blue and Green Infrastructure Potential methods include: Health impact assessments Human and mental health assessments Environmental exposure measurements Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices (KAP) surveys Perception surveys Spatial analysis Ecosystem services accounting Potential supervisors Research Theme A includes supervision from: Prof. Dr. Ina Danquah PD Dr. Timo Falkenberg Prof. Dr. Martin Hamer Prof. Wiltrud Terlau Prof. Dr. Mariele Evers Research Theme B: Urban Disease Ecology The Urban Disease Ecology theme explores how environmental and ecological conditions in urban water landscapes affect disease transmission and human health. The theme is particularly concerned with: Water-borne diseases Vector-borne diseases Infectious diseases Climate-related health risks Water quality Urban morphology Land-use changes Urban density Pathogen transmission Antimicrobial resistance The research takes a One Health approach, recognising the interconnected relationship between human health, animals and the environment. Researchers may investigate how changes in urban development, water management and environmental conditions affect the spread of infectious diseases. Example PhD research topics Antimicrobial Resistance Possible methods include: Microbiological sampling Cultural analysis Molecular analysis Resistance profiling Surveys Water quality analysis Transmission modelling Impact modelling Helminth Infections and Non-Communicable Diseases Potential methods include: Parasitological analysis Microbiological analysis Immunological analysis Clinical examinations Biomarker analysis Mouse models for mechanistic research Urban Microbiome and Dietary Ecology Potential methods include: Microbiome sequencing Dietary pattern analysis Metagenomic analysis Computational analysis Vector-Borne Disease Potential methods include: Climate monitoring Entomological surveys Temperature mapping Vector modelling Pathogen detection Potential supervisors Research Theme B includes: Prof. Dr. Christian Borgemeister Prof. Dr. Achim Hörauf Prof. Dr. Marc Hübner Dr. Indulekha Karunakaran Prof. Dr. Nico Mutters PD Dr. Marijo Parcina Dr. Manuel Ritter Prof. Dr. Marie-Christine Simon Dr. Nicole Zacharias Research Theme C: Governance and Institutional Change The Governance and Institutional Change theme is particularly relevant to applicants interested in policy, governance, economics, development studies, political science, institutional systems and public-sector transformation. This research theme examines how political, institutional and societal structures influence urban transformation and the ability of cities to respond to health and environmental challenges. Areas of interest include: Urban governance Water-health governance Public policy Institutional design Policy instruments Inter-sectoral collaboration Financing mechanisms Participatory decision-making Climate adaptation Population growth Unequal resource distribution Political economy Technological change Healthcare policy Institutional transformation The research seeks to generate evidence that can support more inclusive, transparent and adaptive approaches to urban development . Example PhD research topics Biodiversity-Based Bio-Economies Possible methods include: Economic impact assessment Policy analysis Value-chain analysis Cross-Sectoral Governance Potential methods include: Stakeholder mapping Policy analysis Governance framework development Case studies Urban Transformation and Pharmaceutical Innovation Potential methods include: Case study analysis Technology assessment Policy evaluation Innovation studies Political Economy of Health Equity and Technological Change Potential methods include: Political economy analysis Institutional economics Policy process tracing Case studies Impact analysis Urban Healthcare Policy Implementation Potential methods include: Institutional economics Case studies Impact analysis Microeconometric evaluation Climate-Responsive Health Policy Potential methods include: Policy mapping Infrastructure mapping Spatial analysis Policy evaluation Implementation research Economic impact assessment Potential supervisors Research Theme C includes: Prof. Dr. Katja Bender Prof. Dr. Jan Börner Prof. Dr. Anna-Katharina Hornidge Prof. Dr. Simona Helmsmüller Dr. Christoph Strupat Research Theme D: Adaptive Urban Ecosystems The Adaptive Urban Ecosystems theme focuses on how cities can plan and manage ecological and blue-green infrastructure in response to climate change and socio-economic transformation. Research areas include: Urban land-use systems Water infrastructure Nature-based solutions Ecosystem resilience Climate adaptation Circular economy Integrated water-resource management Biodiversity Urban soil management Ecosystem services Sustainable urban development This theme brings together engineering, ecological and planning perspectives to investigate how urban environments can be designed to provide multiple benefits for both people and ecosystems. Example PhD research topics Coupling Mechanisms of Urbanization Potential methods include: Hydrological modelling System-dynamics modelling Ecosystem-services analysis Biodiversity and Human Wellbeing Potential methods include: Biodiversity surveys Spatial data analysis Socioeconomic surveys Urban Soil Management Potential methods include: Soil sampling Soil biodiversity surveys Morphological identification Molecular identification Soil health indicators Spatial analysis Urban Decision Environments Potential methods include: Coupled ecological-economic systems modelling Collective learning dynamics One Planetary Health Potential methods include: Integrated modelling Framework development Systems thinking Commons governance studies Potential supervisors Research Theme D includes: Prof. Dr. Wolfram Barfuss Dr. Bibiana Betancur Prof. Dr. Lisa Biber-Freudenberger Prof. Dr. Mariele Evers What Does the PhD Programme Offer? Successful candidates will receive a structured doctoral research experience rather than simply conducting an independent PhD project. The programme provides several forms of academic and professional support. 1. Four-Year Doctoral Support Contract The Research Training Group will begin on 1 April 2027 . Successful applicants will receive a four-year doctoral support contract , with remuneration dependent on TV-L pay grade 13 at 65% , in accordance with the German public salary scale. Employment will be at either: University of Bonn; or Bonn-Rhein-Sieg University of Applied Sciences. 2. Funded Research Expenses The programme states that fieldwork, travel and related research expenses are fully funded . This is particularly important for doctoral projects involving international fieldwork or research in different urban environments. 3. Structured Doctoral Training Doctoral researchers will participate in an interdisciplinary training programme covering areas such as: Systems thinking Transdisciplinary research Academic communication Interdisciplinary research Research methods Soft skills Professional development 4. Interdisciplinary Research Environment The programme brings together researchers from different academic disciplines. This allows doctoral candidates to examine urban health challenges from multiple perspectives rather than approaching them from a single discipline. 5. International Research Network Researchers will have access to a strong national and international network involving universities and research institutions in Europe, Africa, Asia and Latin America. 6. Career Development Support The programme also provides dedicated career development support , structured supervision and clear progression criteria. Responsibilities of Selected Doctoral Researchers Successful candidates will be expected to actively participate in the Research Training Group and contribute to its interdisciplinary research environment. Their responsibilities will include: Participating actively in the RTG training programme. Taking part in interdisciplinary seminars. Conducting independent doctoral research aligned with one of the four research themes. Developing appropriate research methodologies. Collecting and analysing research data. Publishing research findings. Contributing to the development of Blue City concepts. Participating in transdisciplinary knowledge exchange. Developing systems-thinking and interdisciplinary research capabilities. Who Can Apply? The programme is seeking applicants who have already completed a Master’s degree or equivalent qualification in a relevant discipline. The call specifically identifies a broad range of eligible academic backgrounds. These include: Agricultural and Food Systems Climate and Earth Sciences Development Studies Ecology and Life Sciences Economics and Management Mathematics Physics Computer Science Environmental Sciences Health Sciences Geography Infectious Diseases Hygiene and Infection Control Medical Microbiology Public Health Urban and Regional Studies Social Sciences Applicants should also demonstrate: A strong interdisciplinary mindset A clear interest in urban transformation Interest in the water-health nexus and/or urban health Excellent written English Excellent spoken English English Language Requirement Applicants are required to provide evidence of English language proficiency at B2 level , according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR), or an equivalent qualification such as TOEFL. Is the Opportunity Open to International Applicants? Yes. The programme has an explicitly international research orientation and involves partner institutions across Africa, Asia, Latin America and Europe . The call identifies partner institutions in Ghana, Togo, Cameroon, Brazil and Japan , while applicants are permitted to propose research sites in any Blue City worldwide . Therefore, the programme is not presented as being restricted to German or European applicants. Applicants should, however, ensure that they satisfy the academic, language and application requirements specified in the official call. Application Documents Required The application process consists of two stages . Applications will first be assessed by the RTG Selection Committee. Candidates considered among the most qualified will then be invited to participate in a virtual interview . Applicants are required to submit the following: 1. Curriculum Vitae A tabular-format CV should be provided, presenting the applicant’s academic background, professional experience, research experience, skills and other relevant information. 2. Degree Certificates and Transcripts Applicants must provide: Higher education degree certificate(s) Full transcript(s) of records An explanation of the grading system used for previous studies 3. Motivation Letter A motivation letter of no more than 500 words is required. The letter should explain the applicant’s motivation for joining the programme and demonstrate their interest in the relevant research area. 4. Research Exposé Applicants must submit a research exposé of no more than 1,500 words . This is an important part of the application because candidates are expected to propose doctoral research aligned with one of the programme’s four research themes. 5. Interdisciplinary Research Statement Applicants must provide an interdisciplinary research statement of no more than 500 words . This should demonstrate their ability to think across disciplinary boundaries and connect their proposed research with the wider objectives of the Research Training Group. 6. Letter of Recommendation Applicants must submit one letter of recommendation . 7. English Language Certificate Applicants must provide evidence of B2-level English proficiency , such as CEFR, TOEFL or an equivalent qualification. Application Deadline The deadline to submit a complete application is: 19 October 2026 Applicants should ensure that all required documents are prepared and submitted through the online application portal before the deadline. Candidates should also indicate the specific research theme they are applying for. Important Information About Gender Equality The call states that, in accordance with the Landesgleichstellungsgesetz (LGG) NRW , women will be given preference in cases where candidates have equal suitability, qualifications and professional performance, unless reasons relating to another candidate prevail. The programme also states that it is committed to diversity and equal opportunity and is certified as a family-friendly university . Why the Blue City Concept Matters The Blue City concept is central to the programme. Rather than treating water solely as something that cities need to control, remove or supply, the programme examines water as an important component of the urban environment. This approach can involve examining: Rivers Coastlines Flood management Water infrastructure Public health Urban ecosystems Climate resilience Green-blue infrastructure Water quality Urban planning Social equity Disease ecology Governance The programme therefore recognises that water-related challenges cannot always be addressed through engineering solutions alone. They may also require changes in governance, public policy, community participation, health systems, environmental management and urban planning. Do you aspire to pursue a world-class doctoral degree at one of Europe’s leading universities while contributing to impactful research that influences economic policy? ETH Zurich is inviting outstanding candidates from around the world to apply for one or more PhD Positions in Applied Macroeconomics and Political Economy at the prestigious KOF Swiss Economic Institute. This doctoral opportunity provides researchers with the chance to conduct cutting-edge empirical research, collaborate with internationally recognized economists, participate in global conferences, and earn a PhD from one of the world’s highest-ranked universities. The positions are designed for ambitious graduates who want to investigate real-world economic challenges using advanced econometric methods and large-scale datasets while developing expertise that can shape future economic policies. Applications are open until 30 September 2026 . About ETH Zurich ETH Zurich is among the world’s leading universities specializing in science, technology, engineering, economics, and innovation. Located in Zurich, Switzerland, the institution has earned a global reputation for: Academic excellence Groundbreaking scientific research International collaboration Policy-relevant innovation Strong industry partnerships With over 30,000 students and researchers representing more than 120 countries, ETH Zurich provides an international environment that promotes independent thinking, innovation, and academic excellence. The university is also home to the internationally respected KOF Swiss Economic Institute , Switzerland’s premier institute for applied economic research. About the PhD Opportunity The Chair of Applied Macroeconomics, affiliated with the Department of Management, Technology and Economics (D-MTEC), is seeking talented doctoral researchers to join its expanding research team. Successful applicants will become members of both: The Chair of Applied Macroeconomics KOF Swiss Economic Institute The program combines academic excellence with policy-oriented research, allowing doctoral candidates to investigate important economic questions that influence governments, international organizations, and policymakers. Rather than assigning fixed dissertation topics, supervisors will work closely with each doctoral researcher to design an individualized research project that aligns with the student’s interests and career goals. Research Areas The research focuses on empirical macroeconomics and policy-relevant economic issues using advanced quantitative methods. Potential research themes include: 1. Globalization and Fiscal Policy Researchers may investigate: Global economic integration International policy competition Fiscal sustainability Government spending Public finance reforms 2. International Taxation One PhD position is specifically aimed at applicants interested in taxation within a global economy. Possible research topics include: Corporate taxation Tax havens Multinational profit shifting International tax competition Political economy of tax rules Labour-market effects of taxation Distributional effects of international taxation 3. Political Economy Possible research areas include: Electoral incentives Political institutions Economic freedom Public policy design Government accountability Information and policymaking 4. Applied Macroeconomics Students may research: Business cycles Inflation Monetary policy Economic forecasting Productivity Long-term economic growth 5. International Economics Topics include: Global trade International markets Cross-border investment Economic integration International policy coordination 6. Migration and Labour Markets Research may examine: Labour-market dynamics Migration economics Household behaviour Employment outcomes Demographic changes 7. Corruption and Governance Candidates may also investigate: Institutional quality Governance reforms Corruption Policy effectiveness Economic development Types of Data Used Researchers will gain experience working with diverse datasets, including: Firm-level data Household data Country-level datasets Administrative data Survey data Geospatial datasets International datasets Text-based datasets Microeconomic databases Macroeconomic databases Research Methods Doctoral researchers will develop expertise in modern econometric methods, including: Panel-data analysis Time-series econometrics Causal inference Quantitative analysis Statistical modelling Forecasting techniques Advanced empirical research methods Responsibilities of Successful Candidates As a doctoral researcher, you will: Develop an original dissertation. Design innovative research projects. Formulate research questions. Conduct empirical analyses. Publish academic papers. Collect and manage research datasets. Document research findings. Present work at seminars. Attend international academic conferences. Participate in workshops. Join research meetings. Complete doctoral coursework. Contribute to limited teaching activities when required. Collaborate with fellow researchers. Supervision Successful candidates will receive academic supervision from: Prof. Dr. Jan-Egbert Sturm Dr. Enea Baselgia (depending on the research area) The supervisory team will provide continuous mentorship throughout the doctoral journey. Academic Environment The Chair emphasizes: Collaboration Academic freedom Research excellence Policy relevance Innovation Interdisciplinary learning Researchers are encouraged to exchange ideas, participate in seminars, and build strong academic networks. Benefits of the PhD Position Successful candidates will enjoy numerous benefits, including: Opportunity to earn a PhD from ETH Zurich. Employment at one of Europe’s leading universities. Membership in the renowned KOF Swiss Economic Institute. Competitive salary according to ETH Zurich regulations. International research exposure. Access to leading economists and researchers. Participation in international conferences. Opportunities to present research globally. Professional mentoring. Career development support. Access to advanced datasets. Strong interdisciplinary collaboration. Research workshops. Academic seminars. Networking with international scholars. Opportunity to build an international academic profile. Potential extension to complete a four- to five-year doctorate. Employment Conditions The successful applicants will receive: Initial appointment of 18 months. Possibility of extension based on satisfactory progress. Expected total PhD duration of approximately 4–5 years. Competitive gross salary under ETH Zurich regulations. Negotiable starting date. Who Should Apply? ETH Zurich welcomes applicants from diverse academic and personal backgrounds. Applicants should have: A completed Master’s degree in Economics or a closely related discipline before the position begins. Strong interest in empirical economic research. Interest in macroeconomics. Interest in political economy. Interest in public finance. Interest in international economics. Strong quantitative skills. Knowledge of econometrics. Knowledge of statistics. Experience using Stata, Python, or R. Excellent English communication skills. Interest in collaborative research. Applicants from quantitative disciplines such as: Statistics Data Science Political Science Finance Public Policy are also encouraged to apply if they possess sufficient economics training. Preferred Skills Although not mandatory, the following are considered advantageous: Panel-data methods Time-series econometrics Causal inference Large microeconomic datasets International taxation Tax competition Fiscal federalism Political economy Research career aspirations German language skills (optional) Commitment to Diversity ETH Zurich strongly promotes: Equal opportunities Diversity Inclusion Respect Academic freedom The university particularly encourages applications from women and individuals from groups traditionally underrepresented in economics. Required Application Documents Applicants must prepare: Letter of motivation explaining research interests. Curriculum Vitae (without a photograph). Writing sample (Master’s thesis, research paper, or equivalent). Complete academic transcript. Copies of degrees and certificates. Contact details of two or three referees. How to Apply Interested candidates must submit their applications through the official ETH Zurich online application portal. Applications submitted by: Email Postal mail will not be accepted. APPLYHERE Application Deadline The deadline to apply is 30 September 2026. Late applications will not be considered. Why You Should Apply This PhD opportunity offers far more than doctoral study—it provides a platform to become part of one of Europe’s most respected economic research communities. Students will gain advanced research skills, publish influential work, collaborate with internationally recognized scholars, and contribute to solving pressing global economic challenges. Whether your ambition is an academic career, work with international organizations, government institutions, central banks, or economic policy think tanks, this doctoral program provides exceptional preparation and international recognition. Visit HERE for more information about the Fully Funded PhD Positions in Applied Macroeconomics and Political Economy at ETH Zurich, Switzerland 2026 Conclusion The ETH Zurich PhD Positions in Applied Macroeconomics and Political Economy represent an outstanding opportunity for talented graduates seeking to build a research career in economics. Through rigorous training, world-class supervision, international collaboration, and access to one of Europe’s leading economic research institutes, successful candidates will develop the expertise needed to influence academic research and economic policymaking worldwide. If you have a strong quantitative background, a passion for applied economic research, and the desire to contribute to evidence-based policymaking, this doctoral program could be the ideal next step in your academic journey. Be sure to submit your complete application before 30 September 2026 . why_it_matches: The research area is deliberately broad and includes the political philosophy of markets, ethics of commodification, consumer duties to buy or invest sustainably, firm and bank duties to mitigate climate change, collective action problems and the philosophy of environmental economics — all of which touch the candidate's ownership/access, consumption, political-economy and post-growth interests from a normative angle.
